cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Hello Dr Green – I’m here to talk to you about my work placement.

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: Oh yes, it’s Holly, isn’t it?

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Yes.

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: So, which work placement have you chosen?

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: I decided to go for the Orion Stadium placement. The event I’ll be managing is one where I’m helping to set up a sports competition for primary school children.

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: Yup. That’s always a popular placement – even though it can be tougher than you think working with children.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: I know, but it’s the fresh air that attracts me – organising something indoors doesn’t have the same appeal (Q21), even though it might be fun.

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: OK, so obviously safety’s going to be one of your key concerns for this event.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Yes, I’ve already thought about that. I’ll need to make sure none of the equipment’s damaged.

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: Ah well, you’ll be working with schools, so the equipment will be their responsibility. However, the grounds and what goes on there will be yours.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Oh I see – that’ll include keeping everyone within the boundary (Q22) once they’re in their kit and on the field?

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: Exactly – you’ll need to inspect areas like changing rooms as well for anything someone can trip over, but your main priority will be not to lose anyone!

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Right. I’ll need staff to help with that.

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: And don’t forget about the spectators.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Mmm. I was thinking that many of them will be parents, who could help run the event.

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: I wouldn’t rely on that. They’ll be more interested in filming their children than volunteering.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: I’ll need to make sure they don’t interfere with events doing that!

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: And that’s not always easy, especially when a proud parent’s trying to get a snap of their child and you want them to move elsewhere. (Q23)

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: OK. What about the scheduling?

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: With sporting events there are all sorts of things that can alter the timetable – like rain, for instance – though so far, we’ve always been lucky with that.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Yeah, and I was thinking about what to do if someone got hurt as well. I know that last year that caused a terrible delay. (Q24)

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: You have to be prepared for such things.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Oh. What if a match ends in a draw – do you let the teams keep going until someone wins?

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: That’ll be up to you – and again, you need to plan for it.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Right.

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: Now, the aim of your work placement is to give you the opportunity to develop the skills that an events manager needs. So, let’s talk about those a bit.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Well, I think my communication skills are pretty good. I can talk on the phone to people and book venues and that kind of thing.

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: Good – just remember it isn’t only about what you say. If you meet someone face-to-face and want to persuade them to be a sponsor, for example … (Q25)

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Oh, I’ll dress up for that! Sure.

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: Good. Let’s go on to think about your organisational skills. You’re working in a very people-based industry and that means things won’t always go to plan.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: I guess it’s being prepared to make changes that matters. (Q26)

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: That’s right. You may have to make an on-the-spot change to a timetable because of a problem you hadn’t anticipated …

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: … just do it! OK

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: How’s your time management these days?

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: I’m working on it – I’m certainly better when I have a deadline, which is why this work suits me.

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: Yes, but it’s how you respond as that deadline approaches! (Q27)

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: I know I’ve got to look calm even if I’m in a panic.

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: Just think to yourself – no one must know I’m under pressure.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Yeah – even though I’m multi-tasking like crazy!

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: Another skill that events managers need is creativity. Often your client has what we call the ‘big picture’ idea, but it’s up to the events manager to think of all the fine points that go to making it work. (Q28)

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Right, so I need to listen carefully to that idea and then fill in all the gaps.

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: That’s right. And you’ll have a team working under you, so another key skill is leadership. Your team may have lots of ideas too, but you’ve got to make the ultimate choices. Do we have refreshments inside or out, for example?

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Isn’t it better to be democratic?

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: It’s a nice idea, but you have the ultimate responsibility. So, believe in what you think best (Q29). Be prepared to say ‘yes’, that’s a good idea but it won’t work here.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: I see what you mean. What about the networking side of things? I know it’s an area that a lot of students worry about because we don’t have much experience to offer others.

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: But even without it – you can still be an interesting person with useful ideas. And the more people you impress, the better.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: I guess that will help me when I apply for a real job. (Q30)

cues.speaker: TUTOR
cues.text: Exactly – think ahead – remember what your ambitions are and keep them in mind.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Definitely.
